## Week 2 Homework

Task:

You need calculate the average percent of science students (in all) grades per county meeting the required standards and produce a map to show where the Country averages are above or below the State of Washington average. **Note** these websites require registration and the data is also on Moodle.

1.  Import packages and libraries
2.  read in data
3.  examine data
4.  join spatial and non spatial data
5.  calculate average percent of science students in all grades per county meeting required standards
6.  create a map to show were county averages are above or below the state average

```{r}
#load in relevant packages/libraries 
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)
library(tmap)
library(tmaptools)
library(sf)
library(readr)
```

# Read the Data In

```{r}
ReportCardData <- read_csv("Report_Card_Assessment_Data_2018-19_School_Year_20241008.csv",
                           locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"),
                           na = c("NULL", "", "NA", "n/a", "#VALUE!"))
```

Datatypelist

```{r}

ReportCardData <- clean_names(ReportCardData)
```

# Data Manipulation & Analysis

Check

```{r}
#check to see what values are stored in the org_level column before next step 
count(science_students, organization_level)

count(science_schools, student_group_type)

count(distinct(science_schools, school_name))
```

### Filter just science students, all grades, only by school per county

```{r}

science_county <- ReportCardData %>%
  select(county, organization_level, grade_level, test_subject, count_of_students_expected_to_test, count_met_standard) %>%
  #filter out non "school" types from organization_level field 
  filter(organization_level == "School") %>%
  # filter just science test
  filter(test_subject == "Science") %>%
  filter(grade_level == "All Grades") %>%
  filter(county != "Multiple") %>%
    group_by(county) %>%
  na.omit() %>%
    ## na.rm = T means remove missing values from the data
    # could also use na.omit or filter greater than 0

  summarise(total_county_met_standard=sum(count_met_standard), 
            total_county_to_test=sum(count_of_students_expected_to_test))%>%
  mutate(percent_met_per_county=(total_county_met_standard/total_county_to_test)*100)

```

```{r}
#test on just adams county to make sure the previous code ran properly
test <- science_county %>%
filter(county == "Adams") %>%
  summarise(total_met = sum(count_met_standard), 
                            total_exp = sum(count_of_students_expected_to_test))
```

```{r}
state_average <- mean(science_county$percent_met_per_county)
  
```

```{r}
#make a column that compares each county value to the state average and some text to say if it is above or below... 

county_only_above_below_state <- science_county %>%
  mutate(difference_to_state=(percent_met_per_county-state_average))%>%
  mutate(across(difference_to_state, ~ round(.x, 0)))%>%
  mutate(above_below = case_when(difference_to_state<0 ~ "below",
                                 difference_to_state>0 ~ "above",
                                 difference_to_state==0 ~ "equal"
  ))
```

# Map Creation

```{r}
# read in the shp
shape <- st_read("Week 2 Homework boundaries-20261021/Washington_Counties_with_Natural_Shoreline___washsh_area.shp")
```

```{r}
plot(WA_county)
```

```{r}
#join spatial and non-spatial data
# the . just means use teh data already loaded
joined_data <- shape %>% 
  clean_names(.) %>%
  left_join(., 
            county_only_above_below_state,
            by = c("countylabe" = "county"))
#keep = true keeps key values from both datasets
```

```{r}

#bbox_county <- joined_data %>%
#  st_bbox(.) %>% 
#  tmaptools::read_osm(., type = "osm", zoom = NULL)

#tm_shape(bbox_county)+
#  tm_rgb()+

tm_shape(joined_data) + 
  tm_polygons(fill="above_below",
              fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(
                values="brewer.bu_pu"),
              fill_alpha=0.5)+
  tm_compass(position = c("left", "bottom"),type = "arrow")+
  tm_scalebar(position = c("left", "bottom")) +
  tm_title_out("Counties above or below state avearge for science in all grades", 
               position=tm_pos_out("center", "top"))
```
